The proposal is the next step of the deprecation work, which wound down low-adoption reserves and instances and deprecated the price feeds of long-tail assets . The proposal covers rsETH, osETH, LBTC, tBTC and rETH on Core, together with a group of lower-exposure reserves. As of 9 November 2026 these assets held $1.33B of collateral backing $1.03B of debt. The initial measure is to freeze each reserve in scope, which stops new supply and sets the LTV to zero while leaving existing positions untouched and unaffected. Reserves that are frozen, or frozen by this ARFC, are borrowable, and still carry more than $20k of debt also have their reserve factor raised to 99%. We will then work with each asset issuer and with the largest borrowers on an orderly migration, and allow positions to unwind naturally before taking any further action. events.excerpt: TL;DR: An opt-in, public, per-account “protected” flag for ERC-20s. Small sends stay instant; anything bigger is scheduled and can be cancelled by a pre-registered backup wallet; a “stress” action sweeps everything to the backup and locks it, which also helps against wrench attacks. Turning protection on is instant; weakening it (off, higher limit, shorter waits, new backup) takes a delay the holder picks. Why: Today a stolen key or a coerced holder means an instant, final drain. Existing approaches are per-transfer (SLOW), need recipient cooperation (ERC-8236), need judges (ERC-20R), protect protocols rather than users (ERC-7265), or only work in one smart wallet. This puts the protection in the token, so it works for any holder and any wallet, including plain EOAs. How it works: protect(backup, dailyLimit, holdWindow, offDelay, lockDuration, fastLane) : instant. Over-limit transferFrom reverts (never returns true without moving tokens, so routers, vaults and lenders can’t be fooled). Over-limit transfer from an EOA may be auto-scheduled, so wallet “Send” buttons just work. queueTransfer → hold window → anyone can executeTransfer ; the owner or backup can cancelTransfer ; with the opt-in fast lane, the backup can approveTransfer to skip the wait. stress(account) : cancels everything pending and moves the balance to the backup, locked for a preconfigured duration (the caller can’t choose it, so a coerced caller can’t pick zero). Receiving is always instant; unprotected accounts are plain ERC-20. Status: We built a working reference implementation at ETHGlobal Mumbai: a 1:1
